lotl.body: The Leafs' season is in the books at the final horn, and the conversation has moved squarely to what comes next. They finished 8th in atlantic division - a final placement that frames every decision this summer. The work now runs through the draft table, the trade market and the cap sheet, and the bets made over the next few weeks will shape the roster that shows up to camp. The next headline here comes from the front office, not the scoreboard. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: A club that was buried by a 16-2 embarrassment one night turned around and answered with punch the next - there's still some backbone here, even if the standings keep telling a harsher story. Toronto's 8-6 comeback over the Cubs on June 20, after the 16-2 drubbing on June 19, was the most important turn in a messy stretch; Daulton Varsho and Kazuma Okamoto each launched three-run homers, and Louis Varland finished with a six-out save, the kind of rescue act that keeps a season from sliding sideways. At 38-39, third in the AL East and 8.5 games back, the Blue Jays are not out of the race, but they are still chasing it with more grit than margin. The 4-3 and 3-0 wins over Boston before the Cubs split suggest a club capable of sudden life, yet the blows to the pitching staff have made every good week feel like it comes with an invoice. Now it's Houston tonight at 6:07 p.m. ET - the next test of whether this surge is a spark or just a brief clean shirt on a soiled week.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The season ended with the hard edge of unfinished business - a 46-36 record, third in the Atlantic, good enough to say the Raptors were relevant and not good enough to say they were safe. The real headline is the growing momentum around a contract extension for Darko Rajakovic, which tells you the club is leaning toward continuity rather than another tear-down-and-rebuild cycle. That makes sense after a year in which Immanuel Quickley reportedly took meaningful strides, even in a strange 2025-26 that never quite settled into a clean identity. The supporting cast still needs sorting out, and Chris Boucher's future matters because he remains the kind of useful, elastic veteran every disciplined roster needs. Toronto finished 10 games back and with a modest 5.0-point profile, a reminder that the gap to true contention was real even when the nightly effort was there. The draft and free agency now become the front office's test of nerve, not panic - and if Rajakovic stays, his voice will shape the answer. Watch the coaching decision first, then the draft board; that's where the next Raptors team begins.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The spring work has given Washington a sharper edge, and the noise around it is all about who can stick when the pads finally come on. K'Lavon Chaisson is already giving the Commanders early reason to believe their gamble was right - the kind of development that matters in OTAs and minicamp, where a roster can turn on one player suddenly looking like he belongs. That is the real story in Ashburn, not last year's old scars. Washington finished 3rd in the NFC East at 6 games back, and the season ended in a W1 finish, but this is a different board now: newcomers are being sorted, schemes are being taught, and every rep is a small referendum on fit. Leo Chenal's arrival, and the reasons he chose Washington, point to a team selling role, clarity and a chance to matter. The Brandon Aiyuk chatter only underscores how hard the Commanders are still trying to add firepower. Watch the defensive front and the receiver room - those are the places where this spring can still change the shape of the season.
